evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: IL-25 injection significantly increased the percentage of eosinophils in the peritoneal lavage of H. polygyrus infected BALB/c mice by day 18.
source: In a similar manner to C57BL/6 mice (Figure 5C and D) IL-25 injection significantly increased the percentage of eosinophils in the PL of H. polygyrus infected BALB/c mice by day 18 (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: 100% of macrophages within the peritoneal lavage expressed RELM-α+ by day 18 in H. polygyrus infected BALB/c mice following administration of IL-25 or PBS control.
source: Within the BALB/c strain, 100% of macrophages within the PL expressed RELM-α+ by day 18 in H. polygyrus infected mice following administration of IL-25 or PBS control, compared to an average of 28% in naïve mice (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Eosinophil and macrophage responses to IL-25 were completely lacking in infected Il4ra-/- mice treated with IL-25.
source: However, these responses were completely lacking in infected Il4ra–/– mice treated with IL-25 (Figure 6C,D), confirming that the IL-25 induced response is itself wholly dependent on IL-4Rα signaling.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6C and 6D.

claim: The IL-25 induced response is wholly dependent on IL-4Rα signaling.
source: However, these responses were completely lacking in infected Il4ra–/– mice treated with IL-25 (Figure 6C,D), confirming that the IL-25 induced response is itself wholly dependent on IL-4Rα signaling.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figures 6C and 6D.

claim: Generation of the type 2 immune response requires sustained interaction and participation of both innate and adaptive immune cells.
source: Generation of the type 2 immune response, and protection from helminth parasite infection, requires sustained interaction and participation of both innate and adaptive immune cells
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to multiple studies (Allen and Maizels, 2011; Grencis, 2015; Harris and Loke, 2017; Van Dyken et al., 2016).

claim: Protection from helminth parasite infection requires sustained interaction and participation of both innate and adaptive immune cells.
source: Generation of the type 2 immune response, and protection from helminth parasite infection, requires sustained interaction and participation of both innate and adaptive immune cells
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to multiple studies (Allen and Maizels, 2011; Grencis, 2015; Harris and Loke, 2017; Van Dyken et al., 2016).

claim: Alarmins such as IL-25 are potent activators of type 2 immunity.
source: Alarmins such as IL-25 are potent activators of type 2 immunity
evidence: This is established knowledge about the role of alarmins in type 2 immunity.

claim: IL-25 plays an important role in stimulating and mobilising effector mechanisms to expel helminth infection.
source: but as we report here, can play an even more important role in stimulating and mobilising effector mechanisms to expel infection.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: Adaptive type 2 responses develop normally in the absence of IL-25R.
source: Specifically, we show that adaptive type 2 responses develop normally in the absence of IL-25R
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Eosinophil and macrophage responses are impaired in the absence of IL-25R.
source: but that eosinophil and macrophage responses are impaired
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1 and 5.

claim: Impaired eosinophil and macrophage responses likely explain compromised helminth expulsion in IL25R-deficient mice.
source: which is likely to explain compromised helminth expulsion in IL25R-deficient mice.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: A requirement for IL-25/IL-25R signaling to expel H. polygyrus has been reported in vaccination models.
source: A requirement for IL-25/IL-25R signaling to expel H. polygyrus has previously been reported in other settings in which Th2 response levels appear unaffected, including both a vaccination model
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Hewitson et al., 2015.

claim: A requirement for IL-25/IL-25R signaling to expel H. polygyrus has been reported following drug-abbreviated primary infection.
source: and following drug-abbreviated primary infection
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Pei et al., 2016.

claim: The resolution of acute N. brasiliensis infection is delayed in Il25-/- mice despite sufficient Th2 cell differentiation.
source: Similarly, it has been reported that the resolution of acute N. brasiliensis infection is delayed in Il25–/– mice despite sufficient Th2 cell differentiation
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Mearns et al., 2014.

claim: Th2 differentiation can occur independently of IL-25R signaling following helminth infection.
source: These results therefore suggest that Th2 differentiation can occur independently of IL-25R signaling following helminth infection
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings and cited literature.

claim: Innate type 2 responses can operate autonomously from adaptive type 2 responses to control parasite expulsion.
source: and reinforce the idea that innate type 2 responses can operate autonomously from adaptive type 2 responses to control parasite expulsion
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Smith et al., 2012 and the experimental findings.

claim: Parasite expulsion requires IL-25R expression on haematopoietic, rather than non-haematopoietic cells in vivo.
source: A wide range of cell types respond to IL-25, but we demonstrated by chimera experiments that parasite expulsion requires receptor expression on haematopoietic, rather than non-haematopoietic cells in vivo.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: In N. brasiliensis infections, intestinal tuft cell-derived IL-25 drives parasite expulsion and the activation of ILC2s in a positive feedback loop mediated by IL-13.
source: In N. brasiliensis infections, intestinal tuft cell-derived IL-25 drives parasite expulsion and the activation of ILC2s, in a positive feedback loop mediated by IL-13
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Gerbe et al., 2016 and von Moltke et al., 2016.

claim: Innate lymphoid cells may not be required for immunity to H. polygyrus.
source: However, our data indicate that innate lymphoid cells may not be required for immunity to H. polygyrus
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Anti-CD90 (Thy1) antibody depletion of ILCs from Rag1-deficient mice did not affect the ability of IL-25 (in combination with IL-4Rα signaling) to expel H. polygyrus parasites.
source: because anti-CD90 (Thy1) antibody depletion of these cells from Rag1-deficient mice did not affect the ability of IL-25 (in combination with IL-4Rα signaling) to expel H. polygyrus parasites.

claim: Both the resident Lin-ST2+CD90hi and the inflammatory Lin-ST2-CD90low ILC populations are depleted following administration of anti-CD90.2 antibody to H. polygyrus-infected mice given IL-25.
source: Through the use of ST2 staining we were able to demonstrate that both the resident Lin-ST2+CD90hi, and the inflammatory Lin-ST2-CD90low ILC populations recently described (Huang et al., 2015) are depleted following administration of anti-CD90.2 antibody to H. polygyrus-infected mice given IL-25.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3 and a citation to Huang et al., 2015.

claim: ILC2 numbers show only modest expansion in the MLN of C57BL/6 mice infected with H. polygyrus.
source: It has previously been noted that ILC2 numbers show only modest expansion in the MLN of C57BL/6 mice infected with H. polygyrus

claim: ILC2 numbers can be considerably boosted following administration of IL-25 in H. polygyrus-infected C57BL/6 mice.
source: and these can be considerably boosted following administration of IL-25

claim: Total ILCs increase with H. polygyrus infection, of which only a small proportion are ILC2s.

source: One explanation is that chronic H. polygyrus infection limits IL-25 and ILC2 expansion by eliciting the production of IL-1β

evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Pelly et al., 2017.

source: Firstly, the expansion of eosinophil and alternatively activated macrophage numbers seen following helminth infection is strongly amplified by IL-25.

claim: Macrophages may represent a major source of IL-13 in H. polygyrus-infected animals.
source: Macrophages may thus represent a major source of IL-13 in infected animals

source: suggesting an element of autologous stimulation through the IL-13-responsive IL-4Rα, which is required for macrophage alternative activation.

claim: The alternative activation of macrophages is critical for immunity to H. polygyrus.
source: The alternative activation of macrophages is critical for immunity to H. polygyrus
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Anthony et al., 2006.
